claim: The v2 remediation empirically resolves all three of my v1 concerns (cost matrix specified, drift decomposed into artifact + real KS signal, seed-variance CI computed) but leaves three load-bearing gaps untouched: concept-drift on P(Y|X), probability calibration, and temporal cross-validation.
evidence: V1 concern #1 (cost matrix) is ADDRESSED: cost_analysis.json specifies FN=$500/FP=$5 with $40,945 savings per 0.4-day slice and is cited by both bull and bear - I accept this resolves the 'missing objective' critique, though I note bear's correct observation that the Bayes-optimal threshold p*=0.0099 implies the current 0.5 threshold is materially under-flagging, which neither side operationalizes.

V1 concern #2 (rel_delta artifact) is ADDRESSED: drift_shuffle.json proves max |rel_delta|=1.9999 under random shuffle, confirming my v1 suspicion that zero-mean PCA features saturate the ratio; the KS test (29/29 significant on Time-median vs 0/29 on shuffle) correctly isolates the real signal - both v2 arguments cite this honestly.

V1 concern #3 (seed-variance) is ADDRESSED: seed_variance.json gives 95% bootstrap CI [0.8554, 0.8764] with both endpoints above the 0.85 bar; the v1 F1=0.8586 was not an outlier (mean=0.8659), so my 'inside noise' critique is refuted - 75% of seeds clear the bar and the CI itself does.

NEW gap #1 (concept drift): KS confirms covariate shift P(X) shifted across Time, but neither argument measures whether P(Y|X) shifted - a model only degrades when the conditional distribution moves, and 29/29 feature shifts could still leave the decision boundary intact. The 'drift monitoring' both sides endorse is still framed on features, not on calibration error or AUC-over-time on labeled slices.

NEW gap #2 (calibration): scale_pos_weight=577 and a Bayes-optimal threshold of 0.0099 (per bear) both depend on predict_proba being calibrated, but metrics.json reports no Brier score, no reliability diagram, and no Platt/isotonic step - the $40,945 EV number assumes the model's probabilities are trustworthy at low thresholds where XGBoost with extreme class weighting is known to be miscalibrated.

NEW gap #3 (temporal validation): the 20-seed study used the SAME stratified 80/20 design repeated with different random_states - all 20 seeds share the iid assumption the KS test just falsified. A time-ordered train/test split (train on first 80% by Time, test on last 20%) would be the strict test of whether the 0.8659 mean survives the very drift both sides acknowledge - it is conspicuously absent.
challenges: Has anyone measured whether P(Y|X) - not just P(X) - shifts across the Time-median split, e.g. by comparing XGBoost AUC trained on first half and tested on second half versus the reverse, to distinguish covariate shift from concept drift?

What are the Brier score and reliability-diagram calibration of predict_proba at thresholds below 0.05, given that bear's Bayes-optimal p*=0.0099 makes threshold-setting entirely a calibration question - and should a Platt/isotonic recalibration step be mandatory before the cost matrix is trusted?

Does F1 under a temporal (non-stratified, Time-ordered) 80/20 split also clear the 0.85 bar, or does the seed-variance CI implicitly launder the very iid assumption the 29/29 KS result says is violated?
